outlines.title: The Psalms
outlines.note: Five books, each closing with a blessing of Yahweh (41:13; 72:18-19; 89:52; 106:48; and Psalm 150 for the last), gathered from the collections of David, the sons of Korah, Asaph and others. A psalm's title stands in the Hebrew text as its first verse or two, and names its author, its kind, its music and at times its occasion.

sections.title: Book One
sections.subtitle: Psalms 1–41
sections.note: Almost all of David; it closes with a blessing (41:13).

sections.title: The gateway
sections.subtitle: Psalms 1–2
sections.note: Two untitled psalms open the whole book: the man blessed in Yahweh's law (1:1), and all blessed who trust in his anointed king (2:12).

sections.title: Psalm 2
sections.subtitle: Yahweh's king in Zion
sections.note: Untitled in the Hebrew; Acts 4:25-26 names David as its author. Quoted of Christ in Acts 13:33 and Hebrews 1:5; 5:5.

sections.title: Psalm 3
sections.subtitle: Many rise against me
sections.superscription: A psalm of David, when he fled from the face of Absalom his son.
sections.note: 2 Samuel 15–18.

sections.title: Psalm 4
sections.subtitle: An evening prayer
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 5
sections.subtitle: A morning prayer
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on the flutes. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 6
sections.subtitle: Rebuke me not in your anger
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; with stringed instruments; on Sheminith. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 7
sections.subtitle: Judge me, Yahweh
sections.superscription: A shiggaion of David, which he sang to Yahweh concerning the words of Cush the Benjamite.
sections.note: Cush is not named elsewhere; a Benjamite, of Saul's own tribe, he was likely one of the men who slandered David to Saul (1 Samuel 24:9).

sections.title: Psalm 8
sections.subtitle: The son of man crowned
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on Gittith. A psalm of David.
sections.note: Hebrews 2:6-9 reads it of Christ.

sections.title: Psalm 9
sections.subtitle: Yahweh judges the nations
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on “The Death of the Son.” A psalm of David.
sections.note: Psalms 9 and 10 make one acrostic, and the Greek Septuagint joins them.

sections.title: Psalm 10
sections.subtitle: Why do you stand far off?
sections.note: Untitled; it carries on Psalm 9's acrostic.

sections.title: Psalm 11
sections.subtitle: In Yahweh I take refuge
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. Of David.

sections.title: Psalm 12
sections.subtitle: Help, Yahweh
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on Sheminith. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 13
sections.subtitle: How long, Yahweh?
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 14
sections.subtitle: The fool says, No God
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. Of David.
sections.note: Psalm 53 gives it again, with God for Yahweh. Romans 3:10-12.

sections.title: Psalm 15
sections.subtitle: Who may dwell on your holy hill?
sections.superscription: A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 16
sections.subtitle: You will not leave my soul in the grave

sections.note: Acts 2:25-31 and 13:35: David spoke of the resurrection of Christ.

sections.title: Psalm 17
sections.subtitle: Hear a just cause
sections.superscription: A prayer of David.

sections.title: Psalm 18
sections.subtitle: Yahweh my rock
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. Of David the servant of Yahweh, who spoke to Yahweh the words of this song on the day that Yahweh delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul.
sections.note: 2 Samuel 22 gives it again.

sections.title: Psalm 19
sections.subtitle: The heavens and the law declare

sections.title: Psalm 20
sections.subtitle: In the day of trouble
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 21
sections.subtitle: The king rejoices in your strength
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 22
sections.subtitle: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on “The Doe of the Dawn.” A psalm of David.
sections.note: Christ's cry from the cross (Matthew 27:46); 22:18 at the cross (John 19:24); 22:22 in Hebrews 2:12.

sections.title: Psalm 23
sections.subtitle: Yahweh is my shepherd
sections.superscription: A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 24

sections.superscription: A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 25
sections.subtitle: To you I lift up my soul

sections.title: Psalm 26
sections.subtitle: Vindicate me
sections.superscription: Of David.

sections.title: Psalm 27
sections.subtitle: Yahweh is my light
sections.superscription: Of David.

sections.title: Psalm 28
sections.subtitle: My rock, be not deaf to me
sections.superscription: Of David.

sections.title: Psalm 29
sections.subtitle: The voice of Yahweh
sections.superscription: A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 30
sections.subtitle: Mourning turned to dancing
sections.superscription: A psalm; a song at the dedication of the house. Of David.

sections.title: Psalm 31
sections.subtitle: Into your hand I commit my spirit
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David.
sections.note: Christ's last words on the cross (Luke 23:46).

sections.title: Psalm 32
sections.subtitle: Blessed is the one forgiven

sections.note: Romans 4:6-8.

sections.title: Psalm 34
sections.subtitle: Taste and see
sections.superscription: Of David, when he changed his behaviour before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed.
sections.note: 1 Samuel 21:10-15, where the king of Gath is Achish: Abimelech was a title of the Philistine kings (Genesis 20; 26). An acrostic.

sections.title: Psalm 35
sections.subtitle: Contend with those who contend with me
sections.superscription: Of David.

sections.title: Psalm 36
sections.subtitle: The wicked, and your faithfulness

sections.title: Psalm 37
sections.subtitle: Fret not because of evildoers
sections.superscription: Of David.
sections.note: An acrostic. The meek shall inherit the earth (37:11; Matthew 5:5).

sections.title: Psalm 38
sections.subtitle: Rebuke me not in your wrath
sections.superscription: A psalm of David, to bring to remembrance.

sections.title: Psalm 39
sections.subtitle: My days a handbreadth
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 40
sections.subtitle: I delight to do your will
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. Of David. A psalm.
sections.note: 40:6-8 in Hebrews 10:5-9, of Christ. 40:13-17 is Psalm 70.

sections.title: Psalm 41
sections.subtitle: Blessed is he who considers the poor
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David.
sections.note: 41:9 in John 13:18, of Judas. 41:13 closes Book One.

sections.title: Book Two
sections.subtitle: Psalms 42–72
sections.note: It closes with a blessing, and with the words: the prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended (72:18-20).

sections.title: Of the sons of Korah
sections.subtitle: Psalms 42–49
sections.note: The Levites descended from the Korah who rebelled (Numbers 16; 26:11), singers in the house of Yahweh (1 Chronicles 6:31-38).

sections.title: Psalm 42
sections.subtitle: As the deer pants
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A maskil of the sons of Korah.
sections.note: Psalms 42 and 43 share a refrain (42:5, 11; 43:5).

sections.title: Psalm 43
sections.subtitle: Send out your light and your truth
sections.note: Untitled; it carries on Psalm 42 and shares its refrain.

sections.title: Psalm 44
sections.subtitle: We have heard with our ears
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A maskil of the sons of Korah.
sections.note: 44:22 in Romans 8:36.

sections.title: Psalm 45
sections.subtitle: The king's wedding song
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on “Lilies.” A maskil of the sons of Korah; a song of loves.
sections.note: 45:6-7 in Hebrews 1:8-9, of Christ.

sections.title: Psalm 46
sections.subtitle: God is our refuge
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. Of the sons of Korah; on Alamoth. A song.

sections.title: Psalm 47
sections.subtitle: God has gone up with a shout
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of the sons of Korah.

sections.title: Psalm 48
sections.subtitle: The city of the great King
sections.superscription: A song; a psalm of the sons of Korah.

sections.title: Psalm 49
sections.subtitle: Man in honour does not abide
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of the sons of Korah.

sections.title: Of Asaph
sections.subtitle: Psalm 50
sections.note: Asaph, David's chief singer (1 Chronicles 16:5-7), a seer (2 Chronicles 29:30). His other psalms open Book Three.

sections.title: Psalm 50
sections.subtitle: The Mighty One summons the earth
sections.superscription: A psalm of Asaph.

sections.title: Psalm 51
sections.subtitle: Create in me a clean heart
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.
sections.note: 2 Samuel 11–12.

sections.title: Psalm 52
sections.subtitle: Why do you boast in evil?

sections.title: Psalm 53
sections.subtitle: The fool says, No God
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on Mahalath. A maskil of David.
sections.note: Psalm 14 again, with God for Yahweh.

sections.title: Psalm 54
sections.subtitle: Save me by your name
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; with stringed instruments. A maskil of David, when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, “Is not David hiding himself among us?”

sections.title: Psalm 55
sections.subtitle: Wings like a dove
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; with stringed instruments. A maskil of David.

sections.title: Psalm 56
sections.subtitle: In God I trust
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on “The Silent Dove of Far-off Places.” Of David. A miktam, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.

sections.title: Psalm 57
sections.subtitle: In the shadow of your wings
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam, when he fled from Saul, in the cave.

sections.title: Psalm 58
sections.subtitle: Surely there is a God who judges

sections.title: Psalm 59

sections.note: 1 Samuel 19:11.

sections.title: Psalm 60

sections.note: 2 Samuel 8:3-14; 1 Chronicles 18. 60:5-12 is taken into Psalm 108.

sections.title: Psalm 61
sections.subtitle: Lead me to the rock
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on a stringed instrument. Of David.

sections.title: Psalm 62
sections.subtitle: My soul waits in silence for God
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 63
sections.subtitle: My soul thirsts for you
sections.superscription: A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.
sections.note: The king of 63:11 is David himself, fleeing Absalom across the wilderness (2 Samuel 15:23-28; 16:2, 14).

sections.title: Psalm 64
sections.subtitle: Hide me from the secret plots
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David.

sections.title: Psalm 65
sections.subtitle: Praise waits for you in Zion
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A psalm of David. A song.

sections.title: Psalm 66
sections.subtitle: Come and see the works of God
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. A song; a psalm.

sections.title: Psalm 67
sections.subtitle: God be gracious to us
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; with stringed instruments. A psalm; a song.

sections.title: Psalm 68
sections.subtitle: Let God arise
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. Of David. A psalm; a song.

sections.title: Psalm 69
sections.subtitle: The waters have come in to my soul
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on “Lilies.” Of David.
sections.note: 69:9 in John 2:17 and Romans 15:3; 69:21 at the cross (Matthew 27:34, 48); 69:25 in Acts 1:20.

sections.title: Psalm 70
sections.subtitle: Make haste to help me
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. Of David, to bring to remembrance.
sections.note: Psalm 40:13-17 again.

sections.title: Psalm 71
sections.subtitle: My hope from my youth
sections.note: Untitled; it follows on from Psalm 70.

sections.title: Psalm 72
sections.subtitle: The king's son reigns
sections.superscription: Of Solomon.
sections.note: Of Solomon, or for him: it prays for the king's son (72:1), and its last verse closes the prayers of David (72:20). The kingdom of Christ.

sections.title: Book Three
sections.subtitle: Psalms 73–89
sections.note: Mostly of Asaph and the sons of Korah; it closes with a blessing (89:52).

sections.title: Psalm 73
sections.subtitle: Surely God is good to Israel
sections.superscription: A psalm of Asaph.

sections.title: Psalm 74
sections.subtitle: Why have you cast us off for ever?
sections.superscription: A maskil of Asaph.

sections.title: Psalm 75
sections.subtitle: When I take the appointed time

sections.title: Psalm 76
sections.subtitle: In Judah God is known

sections.title: Psalm 77
sections.subtitle: I remember the days of old

sections.subtitle: Dark sayings of old

sections.note: 78:2 in Matthew 13:35.

sections.title: Psalm 79
sections.subtitle: The nations have come into your inheritance
sections.superscription: A psalm of Asaph.

sections.title: Psalm 80
sections.subtitle: Shepherd of Israel, restore us
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on “Lilies. A Testimony.” Of Asaph. A psalm.

sections.title: Psalm 81
sections.subtitle: Sing aloud to God our strength
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on Gittith. Of Asaph.

sections.title: Psalm 82
sections.subtitle: God judges among the gods
sections.superscription: A psalm of Asaph.
sections.note: 82:6 in John 10:34-36: the judges of Israel, to whom the word of God came.

sections.title: Psalm 83
sections.subtitle: Keep not silence, O God
sections.superscription: A song; a psalm of Asaph.

sections.title: Of the sons of Korah
sections.subtitle: Psalms 84–88
sections.note: With one of David's (86).

sections.title: Psalm 84
sections.subtitle: How lovely are your dwellings
sections.superscription: For the chief musician; on Gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

sections.title: Psalm 85
sections.subtitle: You have favoured your land
sections.superscription: For the chief musician. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

sections.title: Psalm 86
sections.subtitle: Incline your ear
sections.superscription: A prayer of David.

sections.title: Psalm 87
sections.subtitle: Born in Zion
sections.superscription: Of the sons of Korah. A psalm; a song.

sections.title: Psalm 88
sections.subtitle: My soul is full of troubles

sections.title: Psalm 89
sections.subtitle: I will sing of Yahweh's covenant faithfulness
sections.superscription: A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.
sections.note: The covenant with David (2 Samuel 7), and the throne cast down. 89:52 closes Book Three.

sections.title: Book Four
sections.subtitle: Psalms 90–106
sections.note: Opening with Moses and mostly untitled, it proclaims that Yahweh reigns; it closes with a blessing (106:48).

sections.superscription: A prayer of Moses the man of God.
sections.note: The oldest psalm, from the wilderness.

sections.title: Psalm 91
sections.subtitle: Under the shadow of the Almighty
sections.note: 91:11-12 was quoted to Jesus in the wilderness (Matthew 4:6).

sections.title: Psalm 92
sections.subtitle: It is good to give thanks
sections.superscription: A psalm; a song for the Sabbath day.

sections.title: Yahweh reigns
sections.subtitle: Psalms 93–100
sections.note: The kingdom of God: Yahweh is king, and comes to judge the earth (96:13; 98:9).

sections.title: Psalm 95
sections.subtitle: Today, if you will hear his voice
sections.note: Untitled in the Hebrew; Hebrews 4:7 says God spoke it in David. 95:7-11 in Hebrews 3:7–4:11.

sections.title: Psalm 96
sections.subtitle: Sing to Yahweh a new song
sections.note: 1 Chronicles 16:23-33 gives it, sung when the ark was brought to Zion.

sections.superscription: A psalm.

sections.title: Psalm 100
sections.subtitle: Make a joyful noise

sections.subtitle: Psalms 101–103

sections.title: Psalm 101
sections.subtitle: I will walk with a perfect heart
sections.superscription: Of David. A psalm.

sections.title: Psalm 102
sections.subtitle: The prayer of the afflicted
sections.superscription: A prayer of the afflicted, when he is faint, and pours out his complaint before Yahweh.
sections.note: 102:25-27 in Hebrews 1:10-12, of Christ.

sections.title: Psalm 103
sections.subtitle: Bless Yahweh, my soul
sections.superscription: Of David.

sections.title: Creation and history
sections.subtitle: Psalms 104–106
sections.note: Yahweh's works from creation (104) through the covenant with the fathers (105) to Israel's unfaithfulness and his mercy (106).

sections.title: Psalm 104

sections.title: Psalm 105

sections.title: Psalm 106
sections.subtitle: We have sinned with our fathers

sections.title: Book Five
sections.subtitle: Psalms 107–150
sections.note: The redeemed gathered, the songs of the pilgrim feasts, and a closing crescendo of praise.

sections.title: Psalm 107
sections.subtitle: Let the redeemed of Yahweh say so

sections.title: Psalm 108
sections.subtitle: My heart is steadfast
sections.superscription: A song; a psalm of David.
sections.note: Psalm 57:7-11 and 60:5-12 joined.

sections.title: Psalm 109
sections.subtitle: Let another take his office

sections.note: 109:8 in Acts 1:20, of Judas.

sections.title: Psalm 110
sections.subtitle: Sit at my right hand
sections.superscription: Of David. A psalm.
sections.note: Jesus names David its author (Matthew 22:43-45). The psalm the New Testament quotes most: Acts 2:34-35; Hebrews 1:13; 5:6; 7:17.

sections.title: Twin acrostics
sections.subtitle: Psalms 111–112
sections.note: Each opens with Hallelujah, and each line begins with the next letter of the alphabet: the works of Yahweh, and the man who fears him.

sections.title: Psalm 112
sections.subtitle: Blessed is the man who fears Yahweh

sections.title: The Egyptian Hallel
sections.subtitle: Psalms 113–118
sections.note: Sung at the Passover, remembering the exodus (114:1): after the supper Jesus and the disciples sang a hymn (Matthew 26:30).

sections.title: Psalm 113
sections.subtitle: Who is like Yahweh our God?

sections.title: Psalm 114
sections.subtitle: When Israel went out of Egypt

sections.title: Psalm 116
sections.subtitle: I love Yahweh, for he hears

sections.title: Psalm 117

sections.note: The shortest psalm; 117:1 in Romans 15:11.

sections.title: Psalm 118
sections.subtitle: The stone the builders rejected
sections.note: 118:22-23 in Matthew 21:42, Acts 4:11 and 1 Peter 2:7; 118:26 at the entry into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:9).

outlines.title: The Proverbs
outlines.note: A father's ten lectures to his son, with wisdom's own appeals between them (1–9), then the collections of sayings each headed in the text: Solomon's, the words of the wise, those Hezekiah's men copied out, Agur's and Lemuel's, and the woman of strength.

sections.title: A father's instruction

outlines.title: The Torah portions
outlines.note: The five books of Moses read through in the synagogue in a year, a portion each Sabbath, each named after a word near its start. Moses of old time has in every city those who preach him, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath (Acts 15:21); a reading from the prophets followed (Luke 4:16-17; Acts 13:15).

outlines.title: The law of Moses
outlines.note: The law given at Sinai and repeated in Moab, as the books set it out: the Ten Words and the Book of the Covenant, the tabernacle and its priesthood, the offerings, cleanness and holiness, the laws given in the wilderness, and Moses' sermons on the plains of Moab. The narrative between is left out. The law was a schoolmaster to bring us to Christ (Galatians 3:24), a shadow of good things to come (Hebrews 10:1).
